questions.question_text: The free electrons in metals always obey
questions.answer: Electrons are fermions with half-integer spin and obey the Pauli exclusion principle, thus following Fermi-Dirac statistics.

questions.question_text: At low temperatures, semiconductors will become
questions.answer: At 0K, the valence band of a semiconductor is completely full and the conduction band is empty, meaning no free carriers are available for conduction.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: The quantum of energy in elastic wave is known as
questions.answer: A phonon is a collective excitation in a periodic, elastic arrangement of atoms or molecules in condensed matter, specifically a quantized mode of vibration.

questions.question_text: The acceptor atoms in extrinsic p-type semiconductor contribute
questions.answer: Acceptor atoms create energy levels near the valence band; they accept electrons from the valence band, thereby creating holes in the valence band.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: In a basic OLED structure, the diamine layer is used as a
questions.answer: Diamine derivatives are commonly used as Hole Transport Layers (HTL) in Organic Light Emitting Diodes because of their high hole mobility.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: Electron-Hole pairs are produced due to
questions.answer: Thermal energy provides the necessary excitation for electrons to jump from the valence band to the conduction band, creating electron-hole pairs.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: LED is a semiconductor p-n junction diode which converts ________ under forward bias
questions.answer: A Light Emitting Diode (LED) emits light through electroluminescence when electrical current passes through it in the forward-biased direction.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: A semiconductor has _________ temperature coefficient of resistance.
questions.answer: As temperature increases, more charge carriers are generated in a semiconductor, decreasing its resistance, which defines a negative temperature coefficient.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: The average velocity acquired by the electron in a particular direction during the presence of electric field is called
questions.answer: Drift velocity is the net velocity an electron gains due to the influence of an external electric field.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: The ________ does not require any external energy for process to take place.
questions.answer: Spontaneous emission is a natural decay process where an electron returns to a lower energy state without external stimulation.

questions.question_text: The Ratio of the maximum power that can be extracted from solar cell to the ideal power is called
questions.answer: The Fill Factor (FF) is the ratio of the actual maximum power output (Pmax) to the theoretical power (Voc x Isc).

questions.question_text: The current density is directly proportional to the __________
questions.answer: According to Ohm's law (J = σE), current density (J) is directly proportional to the applied electric field (E).

questions.question_text: An ideal monochromator should have an _________ narrow effective band width
questions.answer: An ideal monochromator isolates a single wavelength, so its effective bandwidth should be infinitely narrow.

questions.question_text: In a _________, the electrons are ejected from a photoemissive surface and are amplified within the cell.
questions.answer: Photomultiplier tubes (PMT) use the photoelectric effect to eject electrons, which are then multiplied via secondary emission through dynodes.

questions.question_text: Alkali metals and their oxides are best ________ materials.
questions.answer: Alkali metals have low work functions, making them excellent materials for photoemissive surfaces (ejecting electrons when exposed to light).

questions.question_text: _________ is used for separating source radiation wavelengths.
questions.answer: A monochromator is an optical device that transmits a mechanically selectable narrow band of wavelengths of light or other radiation.

questions.question_text: The AFM tip should have a radius of curvature of
questions.answer: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) requires a very sharp tip (typically < 10-20nm) to achieve high-resolution imaging of atomic surfaces.

questions.question_text: In a quantum wire, the material size is reduced
questions.answer: A quantum wire is a structure where carriers are confined in two directions and are free to move in only one direction.

questions.question_text: Carbon nanotube reactivity is related to
questions.answer: The chemical reactivity of CNTs depends on their curvature; smaller diameter tubes have higher curvature and higher strain, making them more reactive.

questions.question_text: In CVD chamber, the precursors are introduced to the reaction chamber in the ________ state.
questions.answer: Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) involves chemical reactions of gaseous reactants (precursors) on or near a heated substrate.
